subject: Post-launch overage credits and split invoice flow
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@brightlane.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Siri Patel <siri@brightlane.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 08:14:00 +0000
Subject: Unexpected post-launch consumption — request for credit/split invoice

Lukas,

Thanks for running with us through last week's launch — overall great support from the team. We ran into a larger than expected model usage window between Jun 15–17 and the account recorded ~1.2M tokens over our committed monthly threshold (see attached usage_report_q1.csv). That overage will put us well outside the budget for Q3 unless we smooth it.

Quick asks:
- Can Redwood provide any one-time credit for this overage (we're looking for guidance on what precedent exists)?
- If credit isn't possible in full, would Redwood consider splitting the overrun across the next two invoices to soften the hit?
- We may pursue a short-term quota uplift for future launches — what's the fastest path for a temporary headroom?

CCing Siri on the Brightlane procurement side. Appreciate a quick reply as we finalize our internal Q3 spend.

Best,
Alex Green
Director of Engineering, Brightlane

Attachments: usage_report_q1.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@brightlane.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Siri Patel <siri@brightlane.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected post-launch consumption — request for credit/split invoice

Alex — thanks for flagging and for the usage file. First, congrats on the launch. We expected higher variability for that window but 1.2M tokens is meaningful — apologies for the churn on your finance side.

Proposed immediate path (high level):
1) Temporary, one-off goodwill credit: Redwood can offer an initial one-time credit equal to 25% of the invoiced overage while we reconcile exact metering.
2) Staggered billing: we can spread the remaining 75% of the overage across the next two monthly invoices (50% month-1, 50% month-2) — effectively amortizing the remainder across July/August bills.
3) Short-term quota uplift: if you want a temporary headroom for the next 30 days, we can provision a reserved uplift with a blended rate; I'll attach a draft pricing table for that option.

I've looped in Laura on legal/procurement implications and Ben on pricing — they'll help confirm contract allowances and approval path. If that approach sounds workable, I'll ask legal to prepare a short amendment (DocuSign) and finance to apply the initial credit while the amendment is processed.

Next steps I suggest:
- Laura / Ben: can you confirm any SOW/commit constraints and whether a 25% goodwill credit is approvable without exec sign-off?
- Alex / Siri: if you confirm acceptance, we'll route the amendment and schedule the staggered invoice plan.

Attaching a starting pricing table for the short-term uplift: proposed_pricing_table.xlsx

Thanks —
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: proposed_pricing_table.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@brightlane.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Siri Patel <siri@brightlane.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected post-launch consumption — contract/true-up options

Hi all — running this through procurement/legal and finance. A few notes from our side after a quick review of the account and the current SOW: 

- Contract baseline: Brightlane is on a monthly committed throughput plan (SOW v2.1). The agreement includes a standard true-up clause; one-off credits are discretionary and typically reviewed by the finance lead.
- Quick approval: Ben, do you have latitude to approve a 20–30% goodwill credit for a first post-launch overrun? If yes, we can avoid escalating to the CRO and keep this to an amendments workflow.

Suggested formal resolution (detailed):
- One-time credit: 20% of the invoiced overage applied immediately to your next invoice (Finance will post a credit memo once we confirm final metering).
- Amortization: Remaining overage to be amortized equally across the next two invoices (July and August). We will flag the July invoice with the credit and a line item for the amortized overage.
- Temporary uplift: Provision 30-day headroom at a short-term uplift rate (listed in the attached pricing table). This will be a temporary amendment to the SOW and automatically expire unless you elect to convert to a higher committed tier.

Operational asks for Brightlane:
- Confirm acceptance of the 20% credit and split invoice plan by Thu, Jun 24 so we can route the amendment and lock the July invoice cycle.
- If you want the temporary 30-day uplift, confirm the target daily throughput so we can size the uplift pool.

If you accept, I'll draft the short amendment and Ben will confirm the finance note.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

--
Internal note (to finance/legal): Ben — if you need a backup approver, loop in Marcus Lin.

From: Alex Green <alex.green@brightlane.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Siri Patel <siri@brightlane.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 16:43:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected post-launch consumption — contract/true-up options

Laura / Lukas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear path. Brightlane accepts the 20% one-time credit and the amortization across July/August. We also want the 30-day temporary uplift; target is an extra 600k tokens/day for two weeks starting Jul 1, then reassess.

Please send the short amendment and the DocuSign link so our procurement team can review. Once the amendment is signed, we understand finance will issue the credit memo and the amortized billing will appear on the July invoice.

One request from procurement: can the amendment include a line that we will not be assessed additional penalties if traffic spikes due to post-deployment debugging for 72 hours after a production push? We can include language for a single "post-deploy grace window" per major release.

Appreciate the support — forward the DocuSign and we'll get it signed today.

Best,
Alex Green
Director of Engineering, Brightlane

Attachments: none
